items.title: Professor Longhair (Henry Roeland Byrd) Interview, 1969-05-30
items.q: All these old blues, like Lowell Folsom and Muddy Water and Clean Head Benson, I mean those are really, they're, they're, they're not just somebody helped them up there.

ctx.x: to get back home now. There are a lot of people around there trying to make music what it should be, I think, out there on the West Coast and stuff. Even down here a little, people trying to, they're playing free, you know, they're just, you know, getting that goodwill spread around as much as they can. People playing free all the time because like, they really think, I think too, you know, music ought to be, you know, ought to be something that everybody can enjoy, you know, and if you like the music enough,…

and their 50s and stuff. Yeah. I, I, I, I ain't sat down to myself and I believe that's what's going to happen, you know. All these old blues, like Lowell Folsom and Muddy Water and Clean Head Benson, I mean those are really, they're, they're, they're not just somebody helped them up there. They got up there, I mean for what they knew and what they could do and how the people enjoyed it. Cause I even enjoy it. And if I enjoy a musician, he, he, he, he's got something to offer. Like I said, I enjoy all kinds of…
Uh, mm. I'm trying, trying to think of his last big song. I can't even think of it now.
